summary: Implemented all 5 endpoints this task owns (GET /api/v1/dashboard/summary, GET /api/v1/dashboard/my-tasks, GET /api/v1/dashboard/high-risk-contracts, GET /api/v1/dashboard/filters, GET /api/v1/users) on the Python/FastAPI/PostgreSQL stack CLAUDE.md specifies, reusing the foundation/contracts/counterparties tasks' ORM models (Contract, ContractTask, Counterparty, Tenant, User) and the existing auth/db/error infrastructure unchanged. Added app/schemas/lookup.py (DashboardSummaryResponse, MyTaskItemResponse/MyTasksResponse, HighRiskContractResponse/HighRiskContractsResponse, CounterpartyOptionResponse/OwnerOptionResponse/DashboardFilterOptionsResponse, UserOptionResponse/UserOptionListResponse matching context.json field-for-field, camelCase), app/repositories/lookups.py (tenant-scoped contract counting/listing with the Contract Type/Department/Counterparty/Owner/Date-Range filters, the current-pending-task join for My Tasks, owned-open-contracts for Contract Owner's My Tasks, and distinct-department/counterparty/user lookups for the filter-options and Contract Owner dropdown endpoints), app/services/lookups.py (status-card counts, the UC1-BR-002 overlapping 30/60/90-day expiring-window calculation, the UC1-AF-001/004 empty-tenant vs no-match messaging, the UC1-BR-003/011 My Tasks role branch -- current-pending-step assignee for every role except Contract Owner, who instead sees owned non-Executed contracts -- the UC1-BR-004/010/011 High Risk threshold-and-role-scoping logic with descending risk-score ordering, and the filter-option/Contract-Owner-dropdown assembly), and app/routers/lookups.py wired into app/main.py with per-endpoint require_roles(...) exactly matching the endpoint table (High Risk Contracts excludes SIGNER, GET /api/v1/users is TENANT_ADMIN/CONTRACT_OWNER only). Added 20 new tests (tests/test_lookups.py) against the existing db_client/db_session fixtures: the role/auth matrix (401/403), the empty-tenant and no-match dashboard messages, exact-status counts, the three overlapping expiring windows (20/45/85-day contracts), tenant isolation, My Tasks' current-assignee scoping (including a non-current task being correctly ignored) and Contract Owner's owned-open-contracts scoping, High Risk's default/custom threshold, role scoping, descending ordering and empty message, filter-options staying populated for a zero-contract tenant, and the Contract Owner dropdown's role filter and tenant scoping. `python -m compileall app` and `pytest -q` both pass (114/114, including the pre-existing 94). Verified live against uvicorn: all 5 routes appear in /openapi.json with the right methods, camelCase query parameters and the X-User-Role/X-User-Id security schemes declared; the 401 (missing role header) and 403 (SIGNER on High Risk, LEGAL_REVIEWER on /users, an invented EXTERNAL_PARTY role) matrix behaves correctly end-to-end without a database, since role/tenant resolution happens before any DB dependency runs. Could not verify the DB-backed 200 paths against a live server (no reachable Postgres in this sandbox, same gap T-CONTRACTS-API/T-CLAUSES-API already documented) -- that behavior is instead proven by the 20-test TestClient suite, which exercises the identical FastAPI dependency graph and ORM models through an in-memory SQLite stand-in.

code_files.description: DashboardSummaryResponse, MyTaskItemResponse/MyTasksResponse, HighRiskContractResponse/HighRiskContractsResponse, CounterpartyOptionResponse/OwnerOptionResponse/DashboardFilterOptionsResponse, UserOptionResponse/UserOptionListResponse -- camelCase fields matching context.json exactly, reusing the existing ContractStatus Literal from app.schemas.contract for MyTaskItemResponse.status and adding the equivalent UserRole Literal (including EXTERNAL_PARTY, per context.json's UserOptionResponse.role enum) for UserOptionResponse.role.

Tenant-scoped queries: count_tenant_contracts and list_filtered_contracts (Contract Type/Department/Counterparty/Owner/Date-Range filters shared by summary and high-risk), list_current_tasks_for_assignee (ContractTask JOIN Contract, is_current=true, for My Tasks' reviewer/approver/signer/tenant-admin branch), list_owned_open_contracts (Contract Owner's own non-Executed contracts), plus get_tenant/get_counterparty/list_counterparties/list_distinct_departments/list_users_by_role for the filter-options and Contract Owner dropdown endpoints. No business rules -- data access only.

Business rules: the DashboardFilters value object shared by all three filterable endpoints; status-card counts plus the UC1-BR-002 overlapping 30/60/90-day expiring-window calculation (remaining_days = end_date - today, counted into every window it fits); the UC1-AF-001 empty-tenant message vs the UC1-AF-004 no-match-on-filters message (mutually exclusive, keyed off the tenant's unfiltered total vs the filtered result count); the UC1-BR-003/009/010/012/013 My Tasks branch for every role via current contract_tasks assignment, and the UC1-BR-011 Contract Owner branch (owned, non-Executed contracts) with its own 'You have no pending tasks' empty message; the UC1-BR-004/010/011/013 High Risk threshold (tenant-configured, default 70) and role scoping (Contract Owner limited to owned contracts; Tenant Admin/Legal Reviewer/Approver see the full tenant; Signer is excluded by role list, not by in-service logic) with descending risk-score ordering and its own empty message; and get_filter_options/get_user_options assembling the filter and Contract-Owner-dropdown DTOs.

Thin HTTP binding for all 5 owned routes under /api/v1: dashboard/summary, dashboard/my-tasks, dashboard/high-risk-contracts (role list excludes SIGNER), dashboard/filters, and users (TENANT_ADMIN/CONTRACT_OWNER only, optional role query filter). A shared _dashboard_filters dependency binds the contractType/department/counterpartyId/ownerId/startDate/endDate query params (see blockers) for the three filterable endpoints.
Modified: registered app.routers.lookups.router under the /api/v1 prefix alongside the existing clauses/contracts/contracts_third_party_paper/counterparties routers.

20 tests covering the role/auth matrix (401 missing header, 403 for SIGNER on High Risk and LEGAL_REVIEWER on /users), the dashboard summary's empty-tenant message, exact-status counts, the three overlapping expiring windows, the filters-match-nothing message, and tenant isolation; My Tasks' empty message, current-assignee scoping (including a non-current task being ignored) and Contract Owner's owned-open-contracts scoping; High Risk's default and custom threshold, descending ordering, Contract-Owner role scoping and empty message; filter-options staying populated (Contract Type) for a zero-contract tenant while departments/counterparties/owners stay tenant-scoped; and the /api/v1/users role filter and tenant scoping.

pr.title: feat(uc123): lookups -- dashboard summary, My Tasks, High Risk, filters and Contract Owner dropdown
pr.body: Implements T-LOOKUPS-API: GET /api/v1/dashboard/summary, GET /api/v1/dashboard/my-tasks, GET /api/v1/dashboard/high-risk-contracts, GET /api/v1/dashboard/filters, GET /api/v1/users. Adds the lookups router/service/repository layers reusing the existing Contract/ContractTask/Counterparty/Tenant/User models and the shared auth/db/error infrastructure unchanged -- no new tables, no changes to any other module's code. See blockers for judgement calls: inferred query-parameter filters, the My Tasks Contract-Owner branch definition, the Contract Type filter's static-enum source, My Tasks' dueDate field choice per role, and a sandbox verification gap with no reachable Postgres.

blockers: None of this task's 5 endpoints have an explicit query-parameter list in context.json (only a response_dto per endpoint). For dashboard/summary, dashboard/my-tasks and dashboard/high-risk-contracts I added contractType/department/counterpartyId/ownerId/startDate/endDate query params mirroring the Contract Type/Department/Counterparty/Owner/Date Range Filter names the stories name throughout (UC1-BR-008, UC1-FV-004) and the same naming convention T-CONTRACTS-API already established for its own list filters. startDate/endDate filter on the contract's own start_date >=/end_date <= bounds -- an assumption, since the stories describe a single 'Date Range Filter' without naming which date field(s) it bounds, consistent with the same assumption T-CONTRACTS-API documented. For GET /api/v1/users I added an optional `role` query param (its summary says 'tenant users filtered by role' but context.json names no parameter) so the frontend can request only CONTRACT_OWNER-role users for the dropdown (UC2-BR-003/012); omitting it returns every tenant user.

DashboardFilterOptionsResponse.contractTypes is returned as the fixed, system-wide ContractType enum (the same list CreateContractRequest accepts) rather than data derived from the tenant's existing contracts. UC1-AF-001 requires the Contract Type Filter to be 'displayed and available for interaction even though no data exists to filter' -- deriving the list purely from contract data would make it empty for a brand-new tenant, which reads as broken rather than 'available'. departments/counterparties/owners have no such system-wide enum (department is free-text, counterparties/owners are tenant-created records), so those stay data-derived and can legitimately be empty arrays for a new tenant.

UC1-BR-011 defines Contract Owner's My Tasks panel as 'contracts I own that are awaiting any action, regardless of the specific pending step' but no story spells out which statuses count as 'awaiting action'. I implemented this as every owned contract whose status is not Executed (Draft/In Negotiation/Pending Approval/Pending Signature all count), on the reasoning that Executed is this contract's only terminal, no-further-action status in the DTOs given to this task.

MyTaskItemResponse.dueDate is sourced differently per role branch: for Legal Reviewer/Approver/Signer/Tenant-Admin (the current-pending-step-assignee branch) it is the matching contract_tasks row's own due_date -- the due date for that specific pending step, which the contract_tasks table exists to track. For Contract Owner's 'awaiting any action' branch there is no single current task row to key off (ownership isn't step-specific), so it falls back to the contract's own due_date. No story distinguishes these explicitly; this is the more literal reading of 'due date by which action is required' (UC1-GC-001) for each case.

UC1-AF-005 (redirect to the Login screen with a specific message on session expiry) is one of this task's assigned stories, but there is no session or token concept anywhere in this contract -- CLAUDE.md's Authentication section is explicit that 'there is no login or token flow here' and callers simply assert X-User-Role/X-User-Id on every request. There is no backend state this task could expire, and no endpoint in the endpoint table corresponds to login/session management, so this story has no implementable backend surface under this contract; it is a frontend-only concern (what the frontend does when an API call returns 401) and is left unimplemented here rather than inventing a session mechanism the contract does not name.

Sandbox has no reachable Postgres (connection to localhost:5432 refused), the same gap T-CONTRACTS-API/T-CLAUSES-API already documented. Verified instead: (1) all 5 routes appear in /openapi.json with the right methods, camelCase query parameters and the X-User-Role/X-User-Id security schemes, via a live uvicorn boot; (2) the 401/403 role-matrix live, end-to-end, with no database at all (role/tenant resolution runs before any DB dependency resolves) -- including confirming this exact 500-instead-of-400 gap (a malformed query-param UUID with no DATABASE_URL configured) is pre-existing shared infrastructure behavior already present on the merged contracts module, not a regression introduced here; (3) every DB-backed behavior -- status/expiring-window counts, empty/no-match messaging, My Tasks and High Risk role scoping and ordering, filter-option assembly and the Contract Owner dropdown -- through tests/test_lookups.py's 20 tests against a real FastAPI TestClient wired to an in-memory SQLite session through the identical get_db/current_tenant_id dependency chain production uses.
